h: Treetops, Then a Taste of Chelmsford's Story
p: Hylands Park is no stranger to a crowd. It has hosted big outdoor events and concerts over the years, but on an ordinary weekday it's a calm, spacious place, which makes it an easy spot for a relaxed morning before or after your session. The course takes a good couple of hours, so think of it as the main event and build the rest of the day around it.

If you're new to treetop courses, a few small things make a big difference. Keep your clip-ons in your eyeline, move one step at a time and don't be shy about stopping on a platform to catch your breath. Trainers with a proper tread beat fashion trainers every time, and a light pair of gloves saves your hands on the rope sections.

Not everyone in the family needs to climb. The parkland is wide and open, with woods to explore and plenty of room for running about, so a grandparent with a picnic blanket can have just as good a day.

Chelmsford has a fascinating claim to fame as the home of Marconi's early radio work, and Chelmsford Museum in Oaklands Park tells more of the city's story. For more greenery, Danbury Country Park is a short drive east, and RHS Garden Hyde Hall near Rettendon is a cracking day out for keen gardeners. Writtle, with its pretty village green, is right on Hylands' doorstep for a pub lunch.
